summary: Hipgnosis Songs Fund (HSF) announced that Chair Andrew Sutch will step down and that its 2023 'continuation vote' will likely be held on October 26, though a superior bid in the 'go-shop' period could push it to November. The fund also added a 2026 continuation vote and amended its advisory agreement with Hipgnosis Song Management. This comes amid a 40% discount of share price to operative NAV and a proposed $440 million sale of 29 catalogs to Blackstone-backed Hipgnosis Songs Capital.
one_line: Hipgnosis Songs Fund's chair Andrew Sutch will step down as the fund sets a likely October 26 continuation vote amid a $440 million catalog sale and NAV discount.
key_facts: Hipgnosis Songs Fund (HSF) will likely hold its 2023 continuation vote at its AGM on Thursday, October 26, but it could be adjourned into November.
Chair Andrew Sutch, 73, who has chaired the HSF board since 2018, is stepping down as Chair and director once a successor is hired or before the AGM in Q4 2024.
Director Andrew Wilkinson, 72, intends to retire, reducing the HSF board to five directors.
If shareholders vote to continue, another continuation vote will be held at an Extraordinary General Meeting in January 2026.

On September 14, HSF's market cap was about £1.125 billion, a 40% discount to its operative NAV of $2.316 billion as of end of March; the NAV was calculated by Citrin Cooperman using an 8.5% discount rate.

HSF proposes selling 29 catalogs to Hipgnosis Songs Capital (HSC), backed by Blackstone, for $440 million, a 26% increase on what HSF paid and a 51% premium to the value implied by HSF's market cap for the 30 days ending September 13.
The 'go-shop' clause lets HSF consider rival bids for the 29 catalogs until 11.59pm on October 23; HSM, acting for HSC, has a matching right.
Any superior offer must exceed the aggregate cash net proceeds HSF would receive from HSC's $440 million offer.
Amended Investment Advisory Agreement gives Hipgnosis Song Management (HSM) a 12-month notice period if the IAA is terminated after the 2023 continuation vote.
If HSF's share price averages a discount of 10% or more to operative NAV in January 2025, the board intends to serve notice to terminate the IAA, but may withdraw it during the notice period.
MBW understands HSM would have a first-refusal option to acquire HSF's copyright portfolio if terminated, potentially funded by Blackstone.
HSF posted its best-ever revenues in the 12 months to end of March, and streaming pro-forma revenue rose 14.8% YoY in calendar 2022.
The board cites a 44% total return realised since acquisition on the $440 million transaction.
